title: Agentic Search vs RAG
brief: Developers ask your agent questions about a 2,400-file codebase. Right now a Retriever pastes the 3 code chunks most similar to the question, and the model answers from those. Similar-looking code is often the wrong code, so about half the answers point at the wrong file. Answer at least 85% correctly for under $0.06 per question.

data.name: grep
data.description: Searches every file in the repo for a regex and returns matching lines with path and line number. Use it to find where a symbol is defined or used.

data.name: read_file
data.description: Reads a file, or a line range of it, and returns the text. Use it after grep to see the code around a match.

tasks.label: Webhook retry cap
tasks.prompt: What is the maximum delay between webhook delivery retries, and where is it set?

tasks.label: API key check
tasks.prompt: Which function validates API keys on incoming requests?

tasks.label: Archived rows
tasks.prompt: Why does export_csv skip archived rows?

rag_retrieve.text: Retriever: top 3 chunks by cosine: http/client.py L40-120 "retry with exponential backoff" (0.84), docs/retries.md (0.80), webhooks/models.py L1-60 (0.71).

rag_wrong.text: Retries back off exponentially up to 30 seconds, set in http/client.py line 88. (That is the HTTP client's retry for outgoing API calls, not webhook delivery. It looked the most similar.)

rag_right.text: The retrieved chunks include the right code: the cap is set where the dispatcher schedules retries [webhooks/dispatcher.py].

guess.text: Most frameworks put this in a settings file, probably config/settings.py. (A guess: it never looked.)

browse.text: Listing src/ to get oriented: api/, billing/, export/, http/, webhooks/ ... (no search tool, so it reads the tree)

grep_answer.text: The grep hit says WEBHOOK_MAX_BACKOFF = 3600 in config/settings.py:88, so the cap is one hour. (It never opened the code that uses it: the dispatcher clamps it to 900 seconds.)

agent_answer.text: Webhook retries back off exponentially in src/webhooks/dispatcher.py:142, capped by min(WEBHOOK_MAX_BACKOFF, 900), so 15 minutes. WEBHOOK_MAX_BACKOFF itself is 3600 in config/settings.py:88.

modifiers.note: Similar is not the same as relevant: the HTTP client's retry code looks more like the question than the webhook dispatcher does.
With grep, the model searches for the exact name instead of guessing.
A matching line is not the whole story; without read_file it answers from the grep hit.

hints: Read a wrong answer. The retriever returned code that looks like the question. Is it the code the question is about?
A developer would search for the exact name (MAX_BACKOFF, validate_api_key) and then open the file. Give the agent tools to do the same, wired to the loop.
Add two Tool nodes named grep and read_file, wired to the Agent loop. You can delete the Retriever or leave it; the agent stops relying on it once it can search.
explain: Code has exact names, so an agent that greps for them and opens the file finds the real definition instead of the most similar-looking chunk. It costs a few more turns per question, and there is no index to build or keep fresh.
